newsitem.title: UK: Shell, UK retailers in single loyalty card.
newsitem.headline: Shell, UK retailers in single loyalty card.

text.p: Shell Group said on Wednesday it was linking up with a group of British retailers to launch a single loyalty scheme in Scotland as from Friday.
The scheme, based on smart card technology and scheduled to be expanded into the rest of Britain in the autumn, offers customers discounts on goods and services.
Many other loyalty schemes -- there are about 140 in Britain -- are single company programmes or use the older magnetic strip technology, Shell said.
Loyalty cards have proved to be particularly successful weapons in the fierce battle among British supermarkets to lure away customers from rivals.

Shell's Smart programme has been operational since 1994, but is now being joined by electrical equipment retailer Dixons Group Plc, its units The Link and Currys, as well as insurer Commercial Union Plc and newsagent chain John Menzies.
Other participants are the automobile club RAC, Vision Express, Hilton Hotels and -- from April -- off-licence Victoria Wine.
Shell's arch rival in the UK, British Petroleum Co Plc, already has a nationwide loyalty scheme with retailer Argos and supermarket chain Somerfield Plc, but their scheme uses magnetic strip cards.

The newer smart cards use micro chips and can store cash to make payments or, as in loyalty schemes, discount points received when buying an article. The points entitle customers to buy products at reduced prices from other participants in the programme.
Smart cards have greater storage capacity than the magnetic strip varieties and are also more fraud-resistant.
